text: Common vaccination side effects: animals often lose appetite for a day and run a slight fever; painful swelling or a granuloma can persist for a few days at the injection site. Shock is a more serious reaction (e.g. with the Aujeszky vaccine) — the skin reddens, breathing becomes difficult, salivation increases, and the animal can die; reduce this risk by avoiding stress before/after vaccination, vaccinating in cool early morning hours, and not feeding right before vaccination — inject dexamethasone if shock occurs. Sickness can follow vaccinating an animal that already has a mild, sub-clinical infection (e.g. CSF), causing high temperature, appetite loss, and sometimes death — so it is important to confirm animals are genuinely healthy before vaccinating. Abscesses often result from injecting at the wrong site or with dirty equipment. Mild disease-like symptoms can appear from a live vaccine itself — e.g. a nodule at the injection site with the Fowl Pox vaccine, without severe illness.
